R320 — segmented decode handoff and exposed wait audit
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: read-only source and closed-diagnostic review. W worktree: /home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012, revision nowe3c904e2 (per task owner). No build, test, process, API, device, model, GPU, profiler, Git mutation, cleanup, or source edit. No active run artifacts inspected.

Decision
There is no source-evident safe way to remove the measured GPU-reach wait on the segmented path: each captured segment ends at the point where the host must consume GPU-produced routing/activation data and run the CPU expert service. The 50.27 ms/window “GPU-reach wait” from the closed diagnostic is therefore a composite of GPU work and queue completion to a real host dependency, not established wrapper-only idle time. It must not be counted as wholly removable synchronization cost. A separate, bounded source-level measurement opportunity remains: determine whether per-layer copy-queue drains are no-op on the fixed PCIe=0 path, and conditionally avoid a drain only when an explicit per-segment “no copy issued” proof exists. Do not remove a drain based merely on PCIe=0 configuration.

Evidence in W source
- Segmentation is chosen when host/device concurrent handoff is unavailable, unless explicitly forced (src/core/verify.cpp:415–421). `record_window` cuts the graph at each layer/group boundary where “the host must answer a ring” (1173–1190).
- Each iteration launches a device segment, then calls `stream_sync(cs_)` before reading its sequence and dispatching host CPU experts (1514–1518, 1539–1575). This is a correctness boundary: the host consumes mapped GPU-written data. After host service it publishes flags and launches the next segment (1586–1608). The host cannot safely perform the CPU expert work before those activations/routing data exist.
- `stream_sync` is `rt_of(s).finish(q(s))` (src/core/gpu.cpp:111–114), so timing around it includes queue completion, not just a SYCL wrapper. Queue-empty probing also occurs after initial launch (verify.cpp:1514–1517); no source or measurement establishes that probe as a material component.
- Segmented mode omits device-side flag waits inside `post` (verify.cpp:1136–1147); the host completes the required pool/flag work before launching the successor. Thus replacing queue completion with concurrent volatile/atomic polling would change the established ownership protocol. Do not add such polling: this route was intentionally selected because host/device concurrent handoff is unqualified.
- The per-layer `stream_sync(copy_)` after the pool drains expert-copy work before checking asynchronous callback error and before reusing/publishing staging state (1577–1583). The subsequent `flagB` check and next graph launch rely on that ordering (1599–1607). The fixed PCIe-frac=0 run means no PCIe-share experts, but it does not by itself prove the copy queue is unused by every callback or route. A narrower experiment would first instrument/establish “copy command issued for this segment”; only the branch proven empty could omit that queue drain. Keep all existing completion/error handling whenever a copy was submitted.

Diagnostic interpretation
Closed receipt cited in prior R271 review: 32K input + GEN16, 16 windows, performance_eligible=false; one 124.09 ms/window diagnostic, verify 121.44 ms, GPU-reach 50.27 ms, per-layer host 55.16 ms (CPU 50.64; plan .05, actq .07, jobs .04), stage .49 ms, commit/emit 2.65 ms. These fields are nested/phase diagnostics, not independent costs to sum or subtract. This evidence supports keeping the fixed worker/task sweep as the next performance experiment; it does not show that the 50.27 ms is synchronization overhead. Parent’s forthcoming GEN128 matrix is independent and should remain the only active worker/task run.

Potential work and ranking
1. After the worker/task matrix closes, add diagnostic-only counters around queue finish, copy-queue submission, and CPU callback, plus an explicit per-segment copy-issued bit. Preserve current syncs; collect an unprofiled endpoint A/B first. This verifies whether any empty copy-queue drain exists without changing correctness.
2. If that shows repeatable, nontrivial empty-drain overhead, test only skipping that proven-empty drain. Require byte-identical token output, normal quit and error propagation, repeated clean samples, and unchanged device/route/worker settings. If the copy-issued bit is ever uncertain, always drain.
3. A graph-host-task replacement for explicit cuts is an architecture prototype, not a justified next optimization: prior R271 found graph partitioning inserts runtime-managed synchronization around host tasks, may add overhead, and requires exact deployed-runtime/adapter capability proof. The safe prototype must use stable descriptor slots, serialized replay and unchanged queue/event ownership. Do not use native recording or concurrent host/device polling. Upstream Intel’s graph design and extension documentation describe graph partition/host-task semantics but make no latency claim; there is no evidence it will beat the current explicit cut.
4. Do not try to overlap adjacent layer segments or batch host decisions: the next CPU expert call consumes the previous segment’s output, and each layer’s result feeds the next layer. Multi-window pipelining is separately rejected in segmented mode by verify.cpp:2460; batch windows are rejected at 1787.

Primary references
- Strata source at the pinned W checkout, src/core/verify.cpp and src/core/gpu.cpp (line references above).
- Intel SYCL graph extension: https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_graph.asciidoc
- Intel command-graph design: https://intel.github.io/llvm/design/CommandGraph.html
- Intel Level Zero backend extension (native queue/list and adapter rules): https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/supported/sycl_ext_oneapi_backend_level_zero.md
- llama.cpp SYCL backend (separate backend reference; not evidence about Strata’s route): https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/ggml/src/ggml-sycl/ggml-sycl.cpp

Conclusion
The major exposed wait is attached to a real serialized host-service dependency. Keep it intact. The only defensible nearby target is proving and measuring whether the copy queue is empty at each boundary before considering a narrowly guarded skip; otherwise proceed with the already planned worker/task experiment and retain the current handoff.
